Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J.
1.

Heard Sri Anil Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Kartikey Pandey, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and learned Sri R.K. Srivastava, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.

2. This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.5012 of 2009, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., P.S.- Harraiya, District- Basti.

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was moved on 23.12.2008 by the informant against the applicant and three other co-accused with the allegation that he is neighbour of Prasadi Devi who was issueless, all of sudden her husband Ram Sawaray Lal died and she became owner of the property.

Just to grab her property Sanktha Prasad and Chandradev conspired and got adoption deed in favour of co-accused Sanjay Kumar @ Rinku and Ashok Kumar became witness on the aforesaid deed and forged signature of Prasadi Devi was prepared and on 16.05.1983 it was registered in Gonda and on the basis of adoption deed on 31.08.2000 certificate of the heirship was obtained.
Apart from adoption unregistered Will was also executed by the Parsadi Devi in favour of Sanjay Kumar @ Rinku and Chandradev who are real son of her Devar.
After death of Parsadi Devi on 02.02.2000 the name of Sanjay Kumar @ Rinku and Chandradev was incorporated in revenue record.
Sanjay @ Rinku was also appointed as IVth class employee in education department.
It is also alleged that the adoption deed alleged to be executed by Parsadi Devi is not registered whereas it has been said to be registered.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
He submitted that applicant is only a marginal witness of the will deed in question.

He submitted that after lodging of FIR, the applicant approached before this Court being Application No.32080 of 2022 (Sankatha Prasad and 3 others Vs. State of U.P. and another) for quashing of the FIR on the basis of compromise entered between the parties and this Court vide order dated 09.11.2022 granted interim protection to the applicants provided that the parties shall appear before the Court concerned along with a copy of the order within a week from today and shall be permitted to file an application for verification of the original compromise document, copy of the same is annexed as Annexure No.6 to the affidavit.

entities.text: Sankatha Prasad and 3 others Vs. State of U.P. and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that in pursuance of the order passed by this Court dated 09.11.2022,
the applicant approached before the court below and submitted the compromise deed for verification, which is still pending, and thereafter, the aforesaid application was withdrawn on 21.03.2023, copy of the same is annexed as Annexure No.8 to the affidavit.
He submitted that the said will deed was never challenged before any court.
He submitted that it is a civil dispute between the parties and the present case has been given criminal colour just to harass the applicant.
The applicant is having no previous criminal history as has been mentioned in paragraph 8 of the affidavit.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that applicant has apprehension of imminent arrest and in case, applicant is released on anticipatory bail, he will not misuse the liberty and would co-operate with the trial.
5. Sri Kartikey Pandey, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the applicant.

He has submitted the applicant has committed forge and executed the will deed in question, the will writer was died in the year 1980 and the will was executed in the year 1983, therefore, keeping in view of the seriousness of the allegations made against the applicant, he is not entitled to grant of anticipatory bail.
The apprehension of the applicant is not founded on any material on record.
Only on the basis of imaginary fear, anticipatory bail cannot be granted.

6. Hence without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of applicant, he is directed to be enlarged on anticipatory bail as per Rakesh Kumr Lal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18104701/
2 the Constitution Bench judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal vs. State (NCT of Delhi)- 2020 SCC Online SC 98.

sentences.text:
The future contingencies regarding anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of the Apex Court.
7.
In the event of arrest, the applicant shall be released on anticipatory bail.

Let the applicant-Rakesh Kumr Lal, involved in the aforesaid case crime be released on anticipatory bail on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall co-operate with the Investigating Officer during investigation and shall report to the Investigating Officer as and when required for the purpose of conducting investigation.

( ii) The applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
(iii) The applicant shall not leave the country during the currency of trial without prior permission from the concerned trial Court.
(iv) The applicant shall surrender his passport, if any, to the concerned Court forthwith.
His passport will remain in custody of the concerned Court.
(v) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence and the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law to ensure presence of the applicant.

(vi) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail, the Court concerned may take appropriate action in accordance with law and judgment of Apex Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal vs. State (NCT of Delhi)- 2020 SCC Online SC 98.
(vii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

8. In default or misuse of any of the conditions, the Public Prosecutor/ Investigating Officer/ first informant-complainant is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicant.
